subject: Request: Temporary Dedicated Slice + Autoscale Exception for NovaHealth Pilot
messages:
From: Sana Patel <sana@novahealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Cc: cloudinfra@novahealth.com
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot ask: steady dedicated capacity for 3 weeks

Thanks Michael — quick note from NovaHealth engineering. Our pilot starts next Monday and initial traffic looks spikier than we modeled. We need a small dedicated slice to guarantee latency for our checkout path (PDF generation + Q&A).

Can Redwood provision a temporary dedicated pool of 4 x A100-equivalent slots (or equivalent throughput) for 3 weeks and allow our autoscale policy to exceed the usual per-slate cap during peak windows? We can absorb credits for usage but need the reservation to avoid hard preemption during live demos.

I can jump on a quick call if needed.

— Sana Patel
Director, Platform Engineering
NovaHealth

Attachments: traffic_forecast_q3.csv (CSV, 24 KB)

From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
To: Sana Patel <sana@novahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask: steady dedicated capacity for 3 weeks

Sana — thanks for the heads-up and the forecast. We want to support NovaHealth, but this will require an exception to our safety bands and a short autoscale policy override.

Kimberly / Ops: can we run a quick impact assessment on the requested 4-slot carveout for Sept 6–26 and the proposed temporary autoscale ceiling of +50% during 08:00–20:00 PT? Key asks:
- Total expected tokens/sec equivalent and peak QPS (approx).
- Whether the carveout can be satisfied from a burst lane vs dedicated carved pool.
- Possible mitigations (traffic shaping, pre-warming, fallback model variant).

Sana — I’ll coordinate with Ops and follow up by Monday EOD. I attached a short runbook template so we can capture rollback triggers.

— Michael
Principal Product Manager, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Attachments: nova_pilot_runbook_v1.docx (DOCX, 18 KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask: steady dedicated capacity for 3 weeks

Quick numbers from Ops after an initial probe:
- 4 A100-equivalent slots = ~160 concurrent infer streams at our p50 latency target; peak token throughput ~1.2M tokens/min assuming expected sample lengths.
- We have two candidate fulfillment paths: (A) allocate a temporary carved slice from an underutilized pool in us-west-2 for the 3-week window, or (B) allow burst-lane autoscale up to +50% on existing shared pools. Both have tradeoffs: carveout offers isolation but is harder to revert if other customers ramp; burst-lane is simpler but we could still see preemption if other higher-priority reservations start.

Ops requirements for an exception:
1) A signed mutual action plan from NovaHealth with explicit rollback triggers (traffic thresholds, error rates).
2) A cost/credit agreement for the reserved capacity during the 3-week window.
3) A runbook with automated flux checks and a one-click eviction path (Ops must be able to evict the carveout within 10 minutes).

If Product/AE confirm the willingness for (1)–(3), Ops can provision the carved slice by Friday (4 Sept) and enable a temporary autoscale ceiling. We need explicit approval for the eviction SLA and owner for the one-click button.

— Kimberly
Head of Dedicated Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Sana Patel <sana@novahealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask: steady dedicated capacity for 3 weeks

All — aligned on approach A (temporary carved slice). I confirmed with NovaHealth on the three requirements below and they agreed to sign the MAP:
- Rollback triggers: sustained error rate > 2% or tail latency p95 > 1.5s for 5 minutes.
- Credit agreement: NovaHealth will prepay for the slice at our committed pilot rate; finance has drafted the invoice (linked).
- Runbook: attached (nova_pilot_runbook_v1.docx) — includes automated checks, incident contacts, and the eviction run command.

Jonas, can you please:
- Schedule the carveout for 04:00 PT on Monday 6 Sept (to allow pre-warm)
- Add a temporary autoscale ceiling rule for the slice (+50% between 08:00–20:00 PT) with an automated rollback if any safety metric trips
- Confirm the one-click eviction owner (Ops SRE oncall) and the exact run command for the runbook

Sana — thanks for the quick turnaround on the MAP. We’ll send a final confirmation once Ops validates the provisioning plan.

— Michael

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Sana Patel <sana@novahealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask: steady dedicated capacity for 3 weeks

Provisioning plan executed and smoke-tested:
- Carved slice allocated in us-west-2 (4 A100-equivalent slots) scheduled and pre-warmed at 04:00 PT on Mon 6 Sept.
- Autoscale ceiling set to +50% during 08:00–20:00 PT and bound to the slice policy.
- Eviction path: ops-sre oncall can run "/ops/evict-slice --slice-id=nova-novahealth-20260906 --force"; this action triggers an automated traffic reroute to shared pools as defined in the runbook. Eviction time verified at ~4 minutes.

Monitoring: added a dashboard tile for the pilot with p50/p90/p95 latency, error rate, and token throughput. I will monitor during the first 48 hours and escalate if needed.

Final: Please confirm from Product/AE that the MAP is signed and Finance has processed the prepayment; once we have confirmation we’ll flip the live toggle.

— Jonas
Senior Infra Engineer, Dedicated Runtime
Redwood Inference
